transcript.content: Hello. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm just really struggling with how my face looks, especially my skin. I have these awful acne scars and blemishes that make me feel so ugly, and it's getting to the point where it's completely taking over my life. Other people tell me they can't even see it, but to me, it's just horrible.
Because of these concerns about your skin, do you find yourself spending a lot of time doing things like checking the mirror, trying to hide or camouflage it, or picking at your skin?

Yes, it's honestly exhausting because I'm constantly checking the mirror and spending hours trying to camouflage the flaws with heavy makeup. I also find myself picking at my skin for a long time, desperately trying to 'fix' it, which just makes me feel worse.

Do you experience any other repetitive thoughts or behaviors that are completely unrelated to your appearance, such as excessive handwashing, checking locks, or needing things to be in a perfect order?
No, I don't experience any of those things like excessive handwashing or checking locks. All of my repetitive habits and worries are completely focused on my face and trying to fix my skin.
When you look in the mirror, are you absolutely convinced that your skin is as terrible as you see it, or is there a part of you that thinks your mind might be exaggerating these flaws?

I am absolutely convinced that it looks as terrible as I see it; it's not an exaggeration at all. It is incredibly frustrating when people say they can't see it, because when I look in the mirror, the scars and blemishes are completely obvious and awful. I know what I see, and it's just devastating to look at every single day.
Because of these concerns about your skin, do you find yourself avoiding social situations, work, or going out in public?
I haven't really thought about avoiding those things, to be honest. I just try to get by and do what I need to do, even if it's really hard.
Do you believe there is an underlying medical issue, like an infection or parasites, causing these skin problems, or is your concern strictly about how it looks cosmetically?

No, I don't think there is an infection or anything like that; my concern is strictly about how terrible my skin looks cosmetically. I am just deeply bothered by these awful acne scars and my uneven complexion. I only pick at my skin to try and 'fix' these flaws and make them go away, not because I suspect a medical issue.
How long have you been experiencing these intense worries about your skin and spending so much time on these daily routines?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact timeframe, but it feels like it has been going on for quite a while now. It's hard to pinpoint exactly when it started, but it has definitely been a constant struggle for a long time.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits a severe preoccupation with perceived physical flaws (acne scars and blemishes) that are unnoticeable to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors (compulsive mirror checking, skin picking, and camouflaging with heavy makeup) to correct or hide these flaws. She has absent insight (delusional belief that the flaws are as terrible as she sees them), which is a known specifier of Body Dysmorphic Disorder. She denies other obsessive-compulsive symptoms, ruling out OCD, and her concerns are strictly cosmetic, ruling out somatic delusional disorder. All DSM-5 criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder are met.
